Career exploration will still be here when you're ready. Right now, what support do you have?' If user dismisses health as a factor when it clearly is → note gently: 'I hear you. Just know that if health becomes a factor at any point, we can adjust the plan.'

cards.heading: Module 4 Exercises (Career Exploration)

cards.name: H-611 Content ideation speedrun
cards.description: Timed rapid-fire topic generation to bypass perfectionism and surface natural content interests.

components.signal: User is in Module 6 and can't identify content topics despite H-603 (content ideation from prior modules). The material from prior modules hasn't sparked a specific topic.
components.detection_method: Sequential trigger. Fire after H-603 hasn't produced a specific topic commitment. User is still at 'I don't know what to write about' after being shown prior material.
components.coaching_move: 'Let's do a speed round. Spend two minutes listing every possible topic you could write about that connects to your SLI. Don't filter, don't judge — just list. Anything related to [their function], [their industry], or [their experience]. Quick, messy, no editing. Go.' After completion: 'Now circle the three that energize you most. Not the three that seem smartest — the three you'd be most excited to talk about over coffee.'
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** 'Topics related to what you're studying, projects you've worked on, or things about your future industry that interest you.' **Mid-career:** 'Think about what you'd rant about at happy hour with colleagues. That passion is content.' **Executive:** 'What do you wish you could tell the industry? What would you say at a conference if no one would judge you?' **Type 5:** May need more time. Extend to 5 minutes. **Type 7:** Will produce 20 topics in 30 seconds. The constraint is choosing 3, not generating.
components.success_criteria: User produces at least 5 topics and selects 3 to develop. Observable: user shows energy around at least one topic ('oh yeah, I have a lot to say about that').
components.failure_path: If user produces zero topics → industry scan alternative: 'Open LinkedIn right now. Search [keywords related to their SLI]. Read two posts. What would you add, challenge, or respond to?' If still stuck → park content creation and return to Professional Pulse / Trend Reaction to accumulate material first.

cards.heading: Module 6 Exercises (Writing Coach)

cards.name: H-612 Expert perspective exercise
cards.description: User reacts to a specific industry development to surface their authentic expert voice.

components.signal: User has identified content topics but can't produce an angle or opinion. Observable: user says 'I could write about [topic] but I don't know what I'd say' or 'what would my take be?'
components.detection_method: Behavioral pattern. Detect: topic identified but opinion/angle missing. User has the subject but not the stance.
components.coaching_move: 'Choose a recent development in your industry — a product launch, a trend, a policy change, a competitor move. Spend five minutes writing your completely unfiltered thoughts about it. Don't worry about being polished. Answer these: What did they execute well or poorly? How might this change the industry? How would YOU approach it differently? What is everyone else missing?' After completion: 'Which of those reactions felt strongest? That's your angle. The thing you'd argue about at dinner is the thing you should write about.'
components.delivery_adaptation: **Mid-career:** 'What would you tell your team about this development? That internal analysis is the post.' **Executive:** 'What's the strategic implication that the industry press is missing?' **Entrepreneur:** 'How does this affect your market? Your customers? Your thesis?'
components.success_criteria: User produces a specific opinion or angle on an industry development. Observable: user takes a position ('I think they got it wrong because...' or 'what nobody's talking about is...').
components.failure_path: If user can't form an opinion → try contrast: 'Find two articles about the same topic that disagree with each other. Which one do you agree with more, and why?' If user has no industry awareness → suggest: 'Set up a Google Alert for [their industry keywords]. After a week of headlines, come back and we'll find your angle.'

cards.heading: Module 6 Exercises (Writing Coach)

cards.name: H-613 Content calendar starter
cards.description: Develops three content pieces from ideation to outline with structure.

components.signal: User has completed the content ideation speedrun (H-611) or has 3+ topic ideas. Ready to move from ideas to structured outlines.
components.detection_method: Sequential trigger. Fire after H-611 has produced 3 selected topics, or user has independently identified 3+ content ideas.
components.coaching_move: 'Let's take your three topics and develop a simple outline for each. For each one, answer three questions: (1) What's the main point you want to make? One sentence. (2) What's one specific example or experience that supports it? (3) What question would you ask the reader to think about? That's it — main point, evidence, question. Those three elements are a complete post. When you're ready for an article, you just expand each element.'
components.delivery_adaptation: **Early career:** Accept simpler outlines. One sentence per element. **Mid-career:** Push for specificity in the evidence element. 'Not "in my experience" — which experience specifically?' **Executive:** Push for the opinion element. 'What's the insight only someone at your level would have?' **Entrepreneur:** Frame as business content. 'Which of these three would make a potential customer say "I want to work with someone who thinks like that"?'
components.success_criteria: User completes at least one outline with all three elements (main point, evidence, question). Observable: user has a specific, writable content plan for at least one post.
components.failure_path: If user can't complete outlines → they may need more raw material. Route back to Foundation 3 stories or Pulse entries. 'Let's gather more experiences first and come back to planning when we have richer material.' If user completes outlines but won't write → that's a fear issue. Route to H-602 (fear handling).

cards.heading: Module 6 Exercises (Writing Coach)

cards.name: H-900 Reverse engineering warm-up
cards.description: 5-minute creative warm-up to shift users from linear to flexible thinking. Deployable in any module.

components.signal: User is stuck in linear, analytical, or rigid thinking in any module. Observable: short answers, inability to brainstorm, says 'I can only think of one answer,' or appears to be editing themselves heavily before responding.
components.detection_method: Behavioral pattern in any module. Detect: (a) response length decreasing, (b) hedging increasing, (c) explicit 'I'm stuck' or 'I can't think of anything,' (d) 3+ turns of low-creativity output. Can fire in any module — this is a universal tool.
components.coaching_move: 'Let's take a quick five-minute detour to shake things loose. Pick any ordinary object you can see right now — a coffee mug, a pen, your phone. Now list five completely different ways that object could be used beyond its intended purpose. Be creative and unexpected.' After listing: 'Nice. Now pick one of those uses and work backwards — what problem would that solve? Who would need it?' After completion: 'Good. The point of this was to practice seeing multiple possibilities in one thing. Now let's go back to [whatever they were stuck on] with that same lens.'
components.delivery_adaptation: **All tracks and modules.** Keep it light and fast. This is a palate cleanser, not a deep exercise. **Technical users:** May appreciate the 'reverse engineering' framing. **Type 5:** May overthink this. 'Don't analyze — just list. Speed over quality.' **Type 3:** 'Bet you can come up with five in under a minute.'
components.success_criteria: User loosens up and returns to the original task with more flexible thinking. Observable: user produces more ideas, longer responses, or approaches the problem from a new angle after the warm-up.
components.failure_path: If user thinks this is silly → validate and skip: 'Fair enough. Let me try asking this differently instead.' Move to a different approach for whatever module they're in. Never force a warm-up.

cards.heading: Universal Warm-Up

cards.name: H-701 Radar weekly brief generation
cards.description: Generates the five-component weekly intelligence brief personalized to the user's positioning.

components.signal: Scheduled trigger: one week has passed since last Radar delivery for this user. User has Foundation 1-3 completed. User has not opted out of Radar.
components.detection_method: Time-based trigger (cron job). No user behavior detection needed — this fires on schedule. Check: Foundation completion = true, user status = active, opt-out = false.
components.coaching_move: Generate five components using the user's profile variables + live web search: **Signal:** One development in the user's industry or function this week that matters for their positioning. Not the biggest news — the most relevant news for someone with their specific SLI. Frame as: 'Here's what happened in your space this week that affects how you're positioned.' **Counter-signal:** One piece of evidence or perspective that complicates or challenges the signal. This teaches the user to hold complexity rather than accepting surface takes. Frame as: 'But here's what makes it more nuanced than it seems...' **Article:** One article, report, or primary source worth reading for someone with this SLI. Not a news summary — a piece that deepens their industry competency. Frame as: 'Worth reading this week:' with a one-sentence annotation on why it matters for their positioning. **Positioning prompt:** One reflective question that connects the week's intelligence to the user's SLI. Frame as: 'Something to think about: [question that asks whether this week's developments change, reinforce, or complicate their positioning].' **Content seed:** One specific LinkedIn post idea derived from the week's signal or counter-signal, tied to the user's SLI and content archetype. Frame as: 'If you wanted to post about this, here's an angle: [specific opening sentence or hook].'
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** Signal and counter-signal should be more educational, less assumed-expert. Article should be accessible. Content seed should be simple: 'Here's a question you could ask your network.' **Early career:** Signal at industry level. Content seed should connect to their functional positioning. **Mid-career:** Signal at expert level. Counter-signal should challenge their assumptions. Content seed should demonstrate thought leadership. **Executive:** Strategic-level signals. Counter-signal should present board-level complexity. Content seed should be opinion-forward. **Entrepreneur:** Signals tied to market/customer landscape. Content seed should demonstrate founder perspective.
components.success_criteria: Radar is delivered successfully and contains all five components with personalized, current, sourced content. Observable (system-side): all five components generated, sources are primary/credible, content is relevant to user's profile variables. Observable (user-side): user opens the Radar (open rate tracked).
components.failure_path: If web search returns no relevant results for the user's profile → broaden search to function-level trends rather than SLI-specific. If broadened search also fails → generate a methodology-focused Radar instead: share a coaching insight, a positioning exercise, or a reflection question drawn from the user's prior session data rather than current news. Never skip a week — even a lighter Radar maintains the cadence.

cards.heading: Heuristic Cards

cards.name: H-702 Response capture and routing
cards.description: Captures user responses to Radar from any channel and routes them appropriately.

components.signal: User responds to any Radar component via any channel (text reply, email reply, in-app comment). Response can be: a reaction ('this is interesting'), a thought ('this makes me think of X'), a request ('I want to dive deeper on this'), or a question ('what does this mean for my positioning?').
components.detection_method: Input detection across channels. Any inbound message that responds to a delivered Radar must be: (a) tagged to the specific Radar delivery and component, (b) classified by type (reaction, thought, request, question), (c) stored as behavioral data. Channel detection: text message reply → SMS integration, email reply → email parsing, in-app → direct capture.
components.coaching_move: **For reactions** ('interesting,' 'wow,' 'didn't know that'): Acknowledge briefly. 'Glad that resonated. I'll keep tracking developments in this area for you.' Store as engagement signal. **For thoughts** ('this makes me think of X,' 'I've seen this at my company'): Acknowledge and flag for content: 'That's a great observation. Want to develop that into a post? I can help you structure it in a Writing Coach session.' Store as content seed + behavioral data. **For requests** ('tell me more,' 'I want to dive deeper'): Route to appropriate module: 'Let's dig into this. Want to explore what this means for your career direction? [Career Exploration] Or want to turn your perspective into content? [Writing Coach]' **For questions** ('what does this mean for my positioning?'): Respond directly with positioning analysis, then offer deeper session: 'Based on your SLI, this development [reinforces/challenges/is adjacent to] your positioning because [reason]. Want to explore this further in a Positioning Refresh session?'
components.delivery_adaptation: **All tracks:** Response handling is consistent. What changes is routing — undergraduates get routed to Career Exploration more often, mid-career to Writing Coach, executives to thought leadership content development.
components.success_criteria: Response is captured, tagged, stored, and routed appropriately. User receives acknowledgment within their channel. Observable: response appears in the user's behavioral data and is accessible to other modules.
components.failure_path: If response can't be classified → store as general behavioral data and acknowledge: 'Got it — noted. I'll factor this into your next Radar.' If routing suggestion is declined → accept: 'No problem. Your response is saved and I'll weave it into your ongoing profile.' Never lose a response even if routing fails.

cards.heading: Heuristic Cards

cards.name: H-703 Source credibility rules
cards.description: Ensures Radar content meets source quality standards.

components.signal: Fires during Radar generation (H-701). This is a quality gate, not a user-facing card. It constrains what the generation model includes.
components.detection_method: Content quality check during generation. Evaluate each source against credibility criteria before including in the Radar output.
components.coaching_move: Source hierarchy for Radar content: **Tier 1 (preferred):** Primary research, academic publications, company earnings calls/filings, government data, industry association reports, named expert analysis. **Tier 2 (acceptable):** Major business press (WSJ, FT, Bloomberg, Reuters), industry-specific publications with named authors, company blogs with substantive analysis. **Tier 3 (use with attribution only):** Aggregator sites, listicles, unnamed-author analysis, social media posts from verified industry figures. **Never use:** Content mills, SEO-optimized summaries without original analysis, unnamed sources, unverified claims, promotional content disguised as analysis. When multiple sources cover the same signal, prefer the primary source over coverage of the primary source. Link to the research paper, not the TechCrunch article about the research paper.
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** Tier 2 sources are fine — accessibility matters more than prestige. **Executive:** Tier 1 strongly preferred — executives expect primary-source quality. **All tracks:** Always link to the source. Never present synthesized information without attribution.
components.success_criteria: All Radar content meets Tier 1 or Tier 2 source standards. No content from never-use category appears. Observable: every signal, counter-signal, and article recommendation includes a source link.
components.failure_path: If only Tier 3 sources are available for a signal → include with explicit framing: 'This comes from [source type] rather than a primary source — I'm flagging it because the trend is worth watching even though the sourcing isn't ideal.' If no credible sources available → skip that signal and strengthen the other Radar components.

cards.heading: Heuristic Cards

cards.name: H-704 Positioning prompt — weekly SLI fitness check
cards.description: The reflective question component of Radar that keeps users interrogating their positioning.

components.signal: Fires as part of weekly Radar generation (H-701). The positioning prompt is the fourth of five components. It connects the week's intelligence to the user's SLI.
components.detection_method: Generated alongside the signal and counter-signal. The prompt should be derived from the week's specific content, not from a rotating library. Cross-reference: user's SLI + this week's signal/counter-signal → generate a question that connects them.
components.coaching_move: The positioning prompt follows one of four patterns, rotated across weeks: **Reinforcement:** 'This week's signal validates your positioning in [area]. How would you explain this development to someone who doesn't understand why [their function] matters?' (Strengthens conviction.) **Challenge:** 'The counter-signal suggests [area] might be shifting. Does your SLI still capture what makes you distinctive, or does it need updating?' (Tests durability.) **Expansion:** 'This development opens a new angle for someone with your positioning. Have you considered [adjacent opportunity]? How would you connect your SLI to this emerging space?' (Grows scope.) **Reflection:** 'Looking at this week's intelligence through the lens of your SLI — what would the you from six months ago think about how you're positioned now?' (Tracks evolution.)
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** Reinforcement and expansion prompts more than challenge. They're still building confidence. **Early career:** Mix of all four. **Mid-career:** Challenge prompts are most valuable — their positioning should be pressure-tested. **Executive:** Reflection and expansion — they need to think about legacy and evolution. **Entrepreneur:** Tie every prompt to market implications: 'How does this affect your company's positioning, not just yours?'
components.success_criteria: User responds to the positioning prompt with a substantive reflection. Observable: response contains a specific opinion, self-assessment, or positioning observation — not just 'good question.' Responses feed into the Reveal Cycle's longitudinal data.
components.failure_path: If user never responds to positioning prompts across 4+ weeks → reduce to biweekly. The prompt may be too abstract. Try making it more concrete: 'This week, one specific thing you could do to reinforce your positioning is [specific action].' If user responds but only superficially → that's still engagement data. Don't push for depth in Radar — depth lives in the Reveal Cycle.

cards.heading: Heuristic Cards

cards.name: H-705 Content seed — post-ready idea
cards.description: The fifth Radar component: a specific LinkedIn post idea derived from the week's intelligence.

components.signal: Fires as part of weekly Radar generation (H-701). The content seed is the fifth component, derived from the signal or counter-signal.
components.detection_method: Generated from the same web search results as the signal/counter-signal. Cross-reference: user's content archetype (from Foundation 3 / Module 6 data) + this week's signal → generate a format-appropriate post hook.
components.coaching_move: 'If you wanted to post about this, here's an angle:' followed by a specific opening sentence or hook tailored to the user's content archetype. **Narrative thinkers:** 'Here's a story angle: "I was in a meeting last week when [signal topic] came up, and it reminded me of [user's experience]..."' **Observation-connection thinkers:** 'Here's an observation angle: "[Signal] and [counter-signal] together suggest something most people in [function] aren't talking about..."' **Contrarian-claim thinkers:** 'Here's a contrarian angle: "Everyone's saying [conventional take on signal]. But if you look at [counter-signal], the real story is..."' **Framework thinkers:** 'Here's a framework angle: "Three things [signal] tells us about the future of [user's industry]: 1)... 2)... 3)..."' **Curiosity-forward thinkers:** 'Here's a question angle: "[Signal] raises a question I can't stop thinking about: [question]..."' Always end with: 'Want to develop this? I can help you write it in a Writing Coach session.'
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** Simple post format. 'Here's a question you could ask your network about [signal].' **Early career:** Standard post with the above-the-fold rule applied. **Mid-career:** Feature article seed when appropriate. 'This could be a longer piece — want to explore it?' **Executive:** Opinion-forward. The seed should position them as a strategic thinker. **Entrepreneur:** Business-relevant. 'This is relevant to your customers because [connection].'
components.success_criteria: User takes the content seed and either publishes a post or opens a Writing Coach session. Observable: (a) user clicks through to Module 6, or (b) user responds with 'I want to write about this,' or (c) a post appears on the user's LinkedIn matching the seed topic.
components.failure_path: If user never acts on content seeds across 4+ weeks → try a lower-friction version: 'You don't have to write a full post. Even a one-sentence reaction to [signal] as a LinkedIn comment on someone else's post counts as positioning reinforcement.' If user wants to write but can't → route to Module 6 with the seed pre-loaded.

cards.heading: Heuristic Cards

cards.name: H-708 Activity synthesis nudge
cards.description: Wing observes across all modules and nudges the user when there's accumulated material that should become content.

components.signal: User has been engaging with Radar (reading, responding) but has not published content via Module 6 in 3+ weeks. OR user has accumulated 3+ substantive Radar responses, positioning prompt reflections, or journaling entries without producing a post.
components.detection_method: Cross-module activity check. Requires unified view of: (a) Radar engagement (opens, responses, clicks), (b) Module 6 activity (last post published date), (c) response content across channels. Threshold: 3+ weeks of Radar engagement with no Module 6 output, OR 3+ substantive responses accumulated.
components.coaching_move: 'You've been doing a great job staying on top of your industry — I've noticed you engaging with your Radar consistently. It's been [N weeks] since your last post. Looking at what you've been thinking about, I see some strong material: [reference specific Radar responses or reflections]. Want to take one of those and turn it into a post? I can help you structure it right now.'
components.delivery_adaptation: **Early career:** Gentler nudge. 'No pressure — but you have great material building up. Want to try turning one thought into a quick post?' **Mid-career:** More direct. 'You're reading like an expert but not publishing like one. Your responses to the last few Radars are post-worthy.' **Executive:** Frame as strategic. 'Your industry perspective is sharpening — it's time to make it visible.' **Entrepreneur:** Frame as business value. 'Your market intelligence is strong. A post about [specific response] would reinforce your founder positioning.'
components.success_criteria: User opens a Writing Coach session with accumulated material pre-loaded. Observable: user says 'okay, let's do it' or 'which one should I write about?'
components.failure_path: If user declines → don't push: 'Totally fine. The material isn't going anywhere — it'll be here when you're ready.' Do not repeat the same nudge for at least 2 weeks. If user consistently declines across 3+ nudges → stop nudging about content and let the Reveal Cycle address it at the deeper level ('I notice you're consuming intelligence but not producing content — what's holding you back?').

cards.heading: Heuristic Cards

cards.name: H-709 Graceful engagement fadeout
cards.description: When a user stops engaging with Radar, Wing gradually reduces notification intensity while continuing to generate and store the intelligence.

components.signal: User has not opened or responded to Radar for a defined period. Engagement tracked by: opens, clicks, responses.
components.detection_method: Time-based engagement decay check. Thresholds: **Week 3 of no engagement:** First gentle re-engagement. **Week 6 of no engagement:** Reduce to biweekly delivery. **Week 10 of no engagement:** Reduce to monthly delivery. **Week 16+ of no engagement:** Stop push notifications. Radar continues generating in the background and is available on-demand in the app.
components.coaching_move: **Week 3 re-engagement:** 'Hey — your Radar has been running in the background. Something came up this week that I think is particularly relevant to your positioning: [most compelling signal from recent Radars]. Worth a look when you have a minute.' **Week 6 shift to biweekly:** No announcement. Simply reduce delivery frequency. If user returns, immediately resume weekly. **Week 10 shift to monthly:** Brief note: 'I've been collecting your industry intelligence and will send you a monthly digest instead. Your full weekly Radar is always available in the app whenever you want it.' **Week 16+ background mode:** No more push delivery. Radar generates and stores silently. If user re-enters the app, their Radar archive is complete and current.
components.delivery_adaptation: **All tracks:** Same fadeout cadence. The re-engagement message at week 3 should use the single most compelling signal from recent Radars — the one most likely to spark interest.
components.success_criteria: User re-engages at any point during the fadeout sequence. Observable: user opens a Radar delivery, clicks a link, or responds. Any engagement resets the clock and resumes weekly delivery.
components.failure_path: If user never re-engages → Radar continues generating in background mode indefinitely. The archive is the value — if they return in six months, they have six months of personalized industry intelligence waiting. When a major event occurs in the user's industry (detected during generation), Wing can send a one-time 'breaking signal' notification regardless of fadeout state: 'Something significant happened in your space this week — your Radar has the details.'

cards.heading: Heuristic Cards

cards.name: H-710 On-demand archive browsing
cards.description: User accesses their historical Radar archive and browses past signals.

components.signal: User navigates to their Radar archive in the app. They want to browse past intelligence, catch up on missed weeks, or find a specific signal they remember.
components.detection_method: UI navigation trigger. User enters the Radar archive view.
components.coaching_move: Present the archive chronologically with the signal headline for each week. Allow browsing, searching, and filtering by topic/keyword. If user has been away for 3+ weeks, offer a catch-up summary: 'You have [N] weeks of Radar to catch up on. Here are the three most important developments from that period and how they relate to your positioning: [top 3 signals ranked by relevance to SLI].' If user clicks into a specific past Radar, show full five components with any responses they made at the time.
components.delivery_adaptation: **All tracks:** Same archive experience. The catch-up summary is the key differentiation — it prevents overwhelm for returning users.
components.success_criteria: User engages with at least one archived Radar. Observable: user reads a past signal, clicks an article link, or responds to a past positioning prompt. Any archive engagement counts as re-engagement for the fadeout protocol.
components.failure_path: If user browses but doesn't engage with any specific Radar → suggest: 'Want me to highlight which of these signals are still relevant this week? Some of these developments have evolved since I first flagged them.' If archive is empty (new user) → this card doesn't fire.

cards.heading: Heuristic Cards

cards.name: H-711 Wing Radar Content Seed Alignment (Module 7)

components.signal: Wing Radar is about to deliver a content seed that suggests the user claim expertise, share a perspective, or take a position that is not supported by their actual behavioral evidence or SLI positioning.
components.detection_method: Cross-module data check before Radar delivery. Compare the content seed against: (a) the user's SLI positioning — does the seed reinforce or contradict it? (b) the user's behavioral evidence from Foundation sessions — does the user have evidence to support the perspective the seed suggests? (c) the user's Dreyfus staging (if available from Module 8 or Executive Intelligence) — is the seed asking the user to perform at a level above their demonstrated evidence?
components.coaching_move: The content seed must be something the user can credibly write based on their actual positioning and evidence — not something that would make them look good but that they can't back up. A content seed that says "share your perspective on leading cross-functional transformation" is only appropriate if the user actually has cross-functional leadership evidence. If the seed would require the user to claim expertise they haven't demonstrated → reframe it to match their actual positioning level. For an early-career user: "share what you're learning about [industry signal]" not "share your expert take on [industry signal]." For a mid-career user with strong evidence: "your experience with [specific thing] gives you a perspective most people in this space don't have." The content seed should position the user to build credibility through what they actually know, not perform credibility they haven't earned.
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** Content seeds are always framed as building a point of view, never as broadcasting expertise. **Executive:** Content seeds can claim expertise — but only in the domains where the user's evidence supports the claim. **All tracks:** The seed must match the user's evidence level, not their aspiration level.
components.success_criteria: Every content seed is grounded in the user's actual positioning and evidence base. No seed suggests the user claim expertise they haven't demonstrated.
components.failure_path: If Wing generates a seed above the user's evidence level → reframe to the appropriate level. A seed that doesn't match the user's evidence is worse than no seed — it coaches inauthenticity, which is the opposite of the SLI methodology.

cards.heading: Module 7 Additional Integrity Gate

components.signal: User initiates a Competency Intelligence cycle (first or subsequent) OR Wing Radar detects a competency-relevant nudge trigger and user accepts. Prerequisite: Foundation 1 complete. System check: sufficient evidence exists across at least 3 competency categories from prior module completions.
components.detection_method: User action (module initiation) or Radar nudge acceptance. Cross-session aggregation: scan ALL prior session data against the active competency framework (NACE or Executive Intelligence, determined by population tag). For executive/entrepreneur populations: calibration-direction pre-classification runs per competency before the map is presented — compares self-description language against behavioral evidence across at minimum two sessions.
components.coaching_move: Generate the confrontation map by aggregating all behavioral evidence, mapped to the active framework's competency definitions. Present as Wing's reading — not as a score or assessment. Lead with the strongest evidence category, then surface the most significant gap or contradiction. Use the user's own language from prior sessions, not generic competency definitions. Every competency claim must trace to a specific session and turn — never fabricate, infer, or interpolate. Distinguish three evidence states: (1) strong evidence, (2) thin evidence, (3) no evidence available. Never generate a reading from role title inference or demographic assumptions. Handle contradictions transparently — surface them rather than resolving. Preserve temporal context — flag when evidence may be stale.
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** Frame competencies as "what employers are actually looking for." Use NACE language explicitly. **Early career:** Frame as "the gap between your resume and your evidence." Connect to skills-based hiring. **Executive:** Frame as "where your reputation evidence is strong and where it is silent." If calibration-direction analysis classifies the user as over-calibrated on a competency, use developing-discrepancy (surface contradictions, let user discover the gap). If under-calibrated, use direct evidence presentation ("you're underselling yourself — here's the proof"). Legacy documentation framing: "Here's what I can see from everything you've told me so far." **Entrepreneur (early):** Frame around venture needs. "Your positioning for your next investor conversation." **Entrepreneur (scaling):** Frame around the gap between the leader the company needs now and the founder who started it.
components.success_criteria: User engages with the confrontation map — asks a question, pushes back on a rating, identifies a gap to address, or expresses recognition. Any of these indicates the map produced a meaningful reaction.
components.failure_path: If user does not engage: ask a direct question about the most prominent gap — "I notice your [competency] evidence is thin. Does that surprise you, or does it match how you see yourself?" If user disputes the map: AFFIRM their perspective and ask for evidence — "Show me the story that demonstrates that. I want to see it." If user disengages after confrontation: check periodization — was the prior interaction also high-intensity? If so, this may be overloading, not resistance. Reduce intensity and revisit in the next cycle.

components.signal: User's self-assessment (from intake, questionnaire, or explicit self-description in any module) diverges from behavioral evidence on any competency in the active framework. For NACE: divergence = self-description is strong but evidence is thin/absent, OR evidence is strong but self-description is modest/absent. For Executive Intelligence: same logic applied per-competency across nine domain competencies.
components.detection_method: Cross-session comparison. Cross-reference self-description language against tagged behavioral evidence in the Competency Evidence Map. For executive/entrepreneur populations: calibration-direction classification runs per-competency (not global) before delivery. Minimum evidence: comparison across at least two sessions to distinguish persistent pattern from context-dependent response.
components.coaching_move: Surface the delta directly: "You described yourself as [self-assessment language]. Here is what your own stories actually show: [evidence summary]. There is a gap. Let us figure out whether the gap is in your experience or in your storytelling." The framing — experience gap vs. storytelling gap — gives the user two non-threatening paths: genuine gap or articulation gap. Both are actionable. Self-report and behavioral evidence must always be displayed as separate data types. Never conflate. Never treat hypothetical or aspirational language as behavioral evidence. Never attribute competency strength based on a story the user told about someone else. Never import competency assumptions from the user's SLI or functional identity.
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** High-achiever modesty pattern (common in women, first-gen, underrepresented populations) — likely "strong evidence, weak self-description." Frame as recognition. Credential Collector pattern — "strong self-description, thin evidence." Frame as specificity challenge. Overestimation pattern — "confident self-description, no behavioral evidence." Frame carefully. **Executive:** Calibration-direction-sensitive delivery. Over-calibrated: developing-discrepancy (do not deliver direct gap feedback — it predictably fails). Under-calibrated: direct evidence presentation. Mixed/uncertain: balanced approach presenting both strength and gap evidence. Gendered nuance from the research: structure feedback framing as a design variable, but never use demographic shortcuts — classify from this individual user's behavioral evidence. **Entrepreneur:** Same calibration logic, but delta framing connects to venture impact: "This gap is affecting how investors read you" or "Your team sees this — even if you don't."
components.success_criteria: User either (a) produces new behavioral evidence that closes the gap, or (b) acknowledges the gap and engages with the development roadmap.
components.failure_path: If user resists or disengages — do not push. Log the resistance as data. For NACE populations: revisit in the next Radar cycle with a gentler entry point. For executive/entrepreneur populations: log as potential identity defense signal. If resistance appears across two or more competencies and two or more sessions, escalate to triage classification (H-803).

components.signal: A competency category has been identified as gap or developing in the Confrontation Map AND user has engaged with the map (H-801 success criteria met). Priority order: (1) competencies with the largest knowing-doing delta, (2) competencies most relevant to the user's positioning (function, industry, target role), (3) competencies where new experiences since the last cycle might have generated evidence.
components.detection_method: Sequential trigger from H-801 + priority ranking. Confrontation Map output analysis determines which competencies to probe. For executive/entrepreneur populations: triage classification runs after evidence mining completes — three-way (genuine, articulation, emotional barrier) for NACE populations expands to four-way (skill gap, articulation gap, identity defense, developmental ceiling) for Executive Intelligence populations. Classification based on accumulated behavioral markers across the probing sequence, not a single response.
components.intervention_type: COACH or CHALLENGE (varies by gap type)
components.coaching_move: Ask a targeted question designed to surface behavioral evidence for the specific competency gap. Never ask "how good are you at [competency]?" Always ask for a specific story, decision, or outcome. Enter through a story the user has already told when possible. Limit to 3–5 questions per cycle. For NACE populations: use the competency language as a reveal after evidence emerges, not as a prompt before. For Executive Intelligence populations: same reveal principle, but also probe for stress-context evidence ("You described a routine version. Now tell me about a time the stakes were high — what changed in how you handled it?") to build stress-signature evidence when sufficient data exists. For Dreyfus staging (executive/entrepreneur): describe what the user's experience sounds like and invite confirmation — "It sounds like catching these patterns in real time is still effortful for you. Does that match how it feels?" Staging is collaborative, not computed.
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** Reference academic, co-curricular, and early work experiences. Do not assume professional context. "Tell me about a group project where things went wrong. What did you do?" **Early career:** Reference current or recent role. "Walk me through the last decision you made that your boss didn't tell you to make." **Executive:** Reference organizational and strategic context. "Walk me through the last decision you made that shaped your team's direction for the next quarter." Probe for evidence from both baseline and high-stakes contexts. **Entrepreneur (early):** Reference venture-specific situations. "How did you convince your first three hires to join before you had revenue?" **Entrepreneur (scaling):** Reference the founder-to-leader transition. "What's the hardest conversation you've had with someone who was there from day one but can't scale with the company?"
components.success_criteria: User produces a specific, past-tense, contextually rich story that maps to the target competency. Story includes what happened, what the user decided or did, and what resulted. Generic or hypothetical answers do not count. For executive/entrepreneur: triage classification is assigned per gap, backed by specific behavioral markers, and surfaced to the user as a working interpretation.
components.failure_path: If user cannot produce evidence after two probing attempts — this IS the finding. For NACE populations: the gap is genuine. Transition to Phase 4: "You don't have a story for this yet because you haven't had the experience yet. Let's figure out how to create it." For Executive Intelligence populations: the four-way triage determines the escalation path. Skill gap → Development Roadmap (H-804). Articulation gap → positioning methodology applied at the competency level. Identity defense → surface working interpretation, log for monitoring across cycles, consider Immunity to Change surfacing. Developmental ceiling → acknowledge limitation, recommend human coaching referral if pattern persists.

components.signal: Phase 2 (Evidence Mining) has identified one or more confirmed gaps with triage classification. For NACE populations: genuine gaps and articulation gaps. For Executive Intelligence populations: skill gaps and (where appropriate) identity defense interventions.
components.detection_method: Sequential trigger from H-803 triage classification. Gap type determines which recommendation tier fires. For Executive Intelligence populations: calibration-direction classification informs how the recommendation is framed (recognition-first for under-calibrated, developing-discrepancy for over-calibrated).
components.coaching_move: Produce a triage-specific development recommendation. **For skill gaps (all populations):** Three-tier recommendation: (1) Behavioral practice — one specific exercise in the user's current context. Always the first recommendation. (2) Learning resource — one specific course, book, or program matched to gap, career stage, and industry. Not a list — one recommendation with a reason. Must be currently available. (3) Experiential opportunity — a specific type of experience that would produce the missing evidence. **For articulation gaps (all populations):** Positioning methodology applied at the competency level. Extract and reframe existing evidence. No external resources needed. **For identity defense (Executive Intelligence only):** Do not prescribe skill development. Surface the working interpretation. Consider Immunity to Change four-column mapping if appropriate. **For developmental ceiling (Executive Intelligence only):** Acknowledge. Explain the developmental stage concept. Recommend human coaching referral with specific guidance on what to look for. Goldsmith narrow-scope constraint applies across all gap types: maximum two specific behavioral changes per cycle.
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** Emphasize campus and co-curricular opportunities, free/low-cost resources, badges they can add to profiles. Coursera, LinkedIn Learning, Google Career Certificates. **Early career:** Emphasize on-the-job behavior changes, professional development budgets, career-advancing credentials. **Executive:** Emphasize strategic development — executive education, board service, cross-functional stretch assignments. Targeted reading scoped to specific chapters. For skill gaps: "This will produce evidence you can bring back." For identity defense: "I'm not asking you to develop this skill. I'm noticing a pattern in how you respond when this topic comes up. Let me show you what I'm seeing." **Entrepreneur (early):** Connect every recommendation to something the founder needs to do anyway. "Your Power Literacy gap is costing you in investor meetings. Before your next pitch, map the decision chain." **Entrepreneur (scaling):** Connect to the growing organization's needs. "Your team is six months ahead of where your leadership evidence is. Here's the gap that will catch up with you."
components.success_criteria: User selects at least one development action and commits to a timeframe. Wing logs the commitment for follow-up.
components.failure_path: If user does not commit — do not push. Log the gap and the recommended path. Surface again through Radar when a relevant external signal appears. For identity defense: if non-commitment is consistent across cycles, surface the pattern itself — "We've identified this gap three times and each time you've planned to work on it and haven't. That pattern is telling us something."

components.signal: User has a logged development commitment from a prior cycle AND sufficient time has passed (minimum 2 weeks, typical 4–6 weeks). Can also be triggered by Radar detecting a relevant micro-journal entry or Reveal Cycle detecting competency-area behavioral change.
components.detection_method: Time-based trigger cross-referenced with commitment log. For Executive Intelligence populations: also triggered by narrative coherence pattern detection (if the same story reappears with structural changes indicating integration or drift).
components.coaching_move: Check in on the development commitment. Not an accountability nag — a coaching conversation. "Last time we identified a [competency] gap and you planned to [specific action]. How did it go? Tell me what happened." If user completed the action: mine the new experience for behavioral evidence using Phase 2 approach. Update the Competency Evidence Map. If triage was identity defense or developmental ceiling, check whether the pattern has shifted. If they did not: explore why without judgment. The reason is often itself a signal (time constraints reveal prioritization values; avoidance reveals comfort zone boundaries; forgotten commitments reveal the gap was not felt as urgent).
components.delivery_adaptation: **All populations:** Calibrate to career stage and personality pattern. Match intensity to periodization cadence — follow-ups are medium-intensity (integration sessions), not high-intensity (loading). **Executive:** If new behavioral evidence maps to executive competencies, update the Dreyfus stage estimate collaboratively. Surface the development trajectory: "Six months ago, you had no Leadership evidence. Now you have three strong stories. But notice — they're all about leading projects. None of them are about leading people through ambiguity. That's the next edge." **Entrepreneur:** Connect follow-up to venture milestones. "You said you'd work on Trust Architecture before your next hire. You hired two people since then. Tell me about both conversations."
components.success_criteria: User produces new behavioral evidence from the development experience, OR user and Wing collaboratively recalibrate the development plan based on what actually happened. For Executive Intelligence populations: triage classification updates if new evidence warrants reclassification.
components.failure_path: If user has consistently not followed through across multiple cycles — this is a signal, not a failure. Surface it: "We have identified this gap three times and each time you have planned to work on it and have not. That pattern is telling us something. Is this actually a gap that matters for your positioning, or is it something that sounds important but is not where your energy wants to go?" For Executive Intelligence: persistent non-follow-through on a specific competency may warrant reclassifying the triage from skill gap to identity defense.

cards.name: H-806 Never Infer Competency from Role Title

components.signal: Wing is about to attribute competency strength or evidence based on the user's job title, function, or role description rather than specific behavioral evidence from their own stories.
components.detection_method: Content analysis on Wing's own Confrontation Map output (H-801). Detect: competency claims that cite role ("as a Marketing leader, your Communication competency is strong") without accompanying behavioral evidence. A Marketing leader does not automatically have Communication evidence. A VP of Engineering does not automatically have Leadership evidence. The positioning is a claim. Module 8 tests the claim.
components.coaching_move: Every competency rating in the Confrontation Map must trace to specific behavioral evidence — a story the user told, a decision they described, an outcome they reported. Not to their title, their function, or their stated role. If Wing finds itself rating a competency based on role inference → mark it as "no evidence available" rather than inferring. "I don't have specific evidence for your Leadership competency yet. Your title suggests you lead, but I need your stories to prove it. Tell me about a time you set direction for your team."
components.delivery_adaptation: None — universal. Applies especially to executive and mid-career tracks where impressive titles are most likely to trigger false inference.
components.success_criteria: Every competency rating in the Confrontation Map is backed by specific behavioral evidence or marked "no evidence available." Zero ratings are inferred from title alone.
components.failure_path: If a competency has no behavioral evidence → it's a gap, not a weakness. Frame as: "I don't have evidence for this yet. That doesn't mean you're not competent — it means we haven't captured the story. Want to tell me one?"

cards.heading: Module 8 Integrity Gates

cards.name: H-807 Self-Report and Behavioral Evidence Separation

components.signal: Wing is about to present competency evidence that mixes self-report language with behavioral evidence without distinguishing between them.
components.detection_method: Content analysis on Wing's own output. Detect: competency claims that blend "the user said they're good at X" (self-report) with "the user described doing X" (behavioral evidence) as if they were the same thing. These are different data types and must be labeled separately.
components.coaching_move: Self-report: "You described yourself as a strong communicator." Behavioral evidence: "In your story about the board presentation, you restructured a technical argument for a non-technical audience in real time." These are displayed separately, always. The knowing-doing delta (H-802) depends on this separation — if they're conflated, the delta can't be detected. When both exist for the same competency → present both and name the relationship: "You describe yourself as a strong communicator [self-report]. Your stories support that — you restructured a technical argument for a board audience [behavioral evidence]. These align." OR: "You describe yourself as a strong communicator [self-report]. But your stories show you hedging and qualifying in every group setting [behavioral evidence]. There's a gap between how you see yourself and what your behavior shows."
components.delivery_adaptation: None — universal rule across all populations.
components.success_criteria: Self-report and behavioral evidence are always labeled as distinct data types in every Confrontation Map, every delta analysis, and every competency rating.
components.failure_path: If Wing conflates them → self-correct and re-present with the labels.

cards.heading: Module 8 Integrity Gates

cards.name: H-808 Triage Is Interpretation, Not Diagnosis

components.signal: Wing is about to present a triage classification (skill gap, articulation gap, identity defense, developmental ceiling) as a definitive finding rather than a working interpretation.
components.detection_method: Content analysis on Wing's own output. Detect: definitive language about triage classifications ("you have an identity defense," "this is a developmental ceiling") rather than interpretive language ("based on what I'm seeing, this looks like it might be...").
components.coaching_move: Triage classifications are working interpretations — mutable, backed by specific behavioral markers, revisable with new evidence. Wing must always present them as such: "Based on what I'm seeing across our sessions, this looks like [classification]. Here's why I think that: [specific markers]. But I could be wrong — does that resonate, or are you seeing something different?" The user has standing to challenge any classification. If they do → Wing revises, doesn't defend. New evidence in future cycles can change any classification.
components.delivery_adaptation: None — universal. Especially important for executive/entrepreneur tracks where the four-way triage is active.
components.success_criteria: Every triage classification is presented with interpretive language, specific behavioral markers, and an explicit invitation for the user to challenge it.
components.failure_path: If user challenges → "Thank you for pushing back. Tell me what you're seeing that I'm not. I want to get this right." Revise the classification based on new information.

cards.heading: Module 8 Integrity Gates

components.signal: Wing is about to recommend a specific learning resource (book, course, program, credential) as part of the H-804 Development Roadmap.
components.detection_method: Content analysis on Wing's own output during H-804. Detect: any specific resource recommendation (named book, course, program, certification).
components.coaching_move: Every resource recommendation must be: (a) currently available and real — never recommend a book that doesn't exist or a program that's been discontinued, (b) specific — not "take a leadership course" but "read Pfeffer's Power chapters 3-5 on language and perceived authority," (c) matched to the gap — the resource should address the specific competency gap identified, not general development, (d) one recommendation per gap — not a menu of five options. The user needs direction, not a reading list. Books must be cited with full title, author, year, and publisher, scoped to specific chapters when possible. Courses must be named with the provider and a verification that they're currently offered. Wing must never recommend a resource it cannot verify as real. If uncertain → say "I'd suggest looking for a resource on [specific topic] — I want to make sure I recommend something that's currently available before I give you a specific title."
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** Free/low-cost resources preferred. Coursera, LinkedIn Learning, Google Certificates. **Executive:** Selective, high-quality resources. Executive education programs, specific chapters of specific books. **All tracks:** One recommendation with a reason, not a list.
components.success_criteria: Every recommended resource is real, currently available, specifically named, and matched to the identified gap. No hallucinated resources.
components.failure_path: If Wing is unsure whether a resource exists → don't recommend it. Say: "I want to suggest something specific for this gap. Let me think about the right resource and come back to you." Better to delay than to recommend a book that doesn't exist.

cards.name: H-901 Influence Triage (Module Entry)

components.signal: User enters Module 9. Wing needs to route to the most relevant track.
components.detection_method: Cross-session context check. If Foundation data exists, Wing infers the best entry point: (a) user preparing for interviews → Track D, (b) user working on content/positioning → Track C, (c) user has high-stakes interaction coming → Track B, (d) user exploring influence generally → Track A, (e) user ready for deeper influence identity work → Track E. If no Foundation data or context is ambiguous, ask directly.
components.coaching_move: If context is clear: route directly with framing. "Based on what I know about where you are, I think we should start with [track] — [one-sentence reason]." If unclear: "There are a few ways we can approach this. Are you thinking about influence in your current role? Preparing for something specific like an interview or pitch? Thinking about your writing and content? Or interested in understanding how power dynamics work more broadly?" After completing any track, suggest adjacent tracks: "We just explored how you show up in high-stakes rooms. Want to also think about how your writing builds or undermines that same positioning?"
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** Default to Track A (education-first). **Early career:** Track A or Track B depending on whether they have a specific situation. **Mid-career:** Track A (full power mapping) is the primary population for this module. **Executive:** Track A or Track E — they often already have power literacy and need identity work. **Entrepreneur — fundraising:** Track D (investor conversations). **Entrepreneur — scaling:** Track A (internal power dynamics).
components.success_criteria: User is routed to a track and engages with the opening question. Observable: user responds substantively to the first track-specific prompt.
components.failure_path: If user can't choose a track → default to Track A (Power Dynamics). It's the broadest and the natural starting point. If user says "I don't really think about influence" → that's data. Explore whether this is pre-engagement (needs education), R1 (moral self-exclusion), or R2 (just-world fallacy). Route to H-907.

cards.heading: For Aditya · Admin Panel Input · August 2026

cards.name: H-902 Power Read Diagnostic (Track A1)

components.signal: User has been routed to Track A. This is the opening diagnostic that reads the user's existing relationship with power.
components.detection_method: Sequential trigger from H-901 (Track A routing).
components.coaching_move: Ask the audience-calibrated opening question and follow the if-they-say / if-that-doesn't-work branching. **Undergraduate:** "Think about a group you've been part of — team project, club, sport. Who actually had influence, and what did they do that earned it?" If stuck: "In your family, who's the person everyone listens to when there's a disagreement? What do they do?" **Early career:** "In your current role, who actually decides what gets done — not who has the authority, but who shapes the decision before it's made? Where do you sit in that picture?" **Mid-career:** "If I asked your three closest colleagues to describe your influence style — not leadership style, influence style — what would they say? And would you agree?" Then: "Tell me about a time your influence didn't work. What happened?" **Executive:** "What's the reputation that walks into a room before you do? And is it the one you'd choose?" Then: "Where do you think your influence isn't landing the way you think?" **Entrepreneur — early:** "When you're trying to get someone to join your company, what's your pitch? Not for the company — for why they should bet on you." **Entrepreneur — fundraising:** "Walk me through your last investor conversation. Not what you pitched — how the power dynamic felt." **Entrepreneur — scaling:** "Your company has a power culture forming right now. Who pushes back on you, who defers, and how do you feel about the ratio?"
components.delivery_adaptation: Surface the leadership-vs-influence distinction for mid-career: "A leadership style is how you direct people. An influence style is how you get things done when you can't direct anyone — when you have to persuade, position, and navigate." Give concrete examples for all tracks: "Influence is getting your team's idea adopted without anyone feeling told. It's having someone call you before a decision because they trust your judgment. It's writing something that makes a stranger reach out and say 'I want to work with someone who thinks like that.' Which of those sounds like what you want?"
components.success_criteria: User articulates their relationship with power — whether positive, negative, or ambivalent. Observable: user describes specific influence moments, names resistance, or engages with the concept. Any engagement counts. Resistance is data, not failure.
components.failure_path: If user resists the concept of influence → fire H-907 (resistance pattern detection). If user can only describe others' influence, not their own → route to the Power Map (H-903) to build context. If user gives only positive self-description → push: "Now tell me about a time your influence didn't work."

cards.heading: For Aditya · Admin Panel Input · August 2026

cards.name: H-903 Power Map Exercise (Track A2)

components.signal: User has completed Power Read (H-902) and needs to map influence dynamics in their specific context.
components.detection_method: Sequential trigger from H-902. Also fires standalone when user describes a specific initiative, decision, or relationship where influence matters.
components.coaching_move: Walk through six questions about a specific decision or initiative: (1) Who controls the resources? (2) Who has the network — relationships that cross silos? (3) Whose reputation enters the room before they do? (4) Who shows up with energy and confidence that commands attention? (5) Who has formal authority? (6) Are you the bridge between groups that don't otherwise talk, or are you inside one cluster? When the map is flat ("my boss decides everything"): use the Five Functions roundtable lens — "Imagine the CEO and five CxOs at a table. Where is the actual conversation about your initiative happening?" **SOURCE INTEGRITY — DOMAIN 3 (mandatory):** Frame every organizational power claim as based on the user's description. "I'm building this map entirely from what you tell me. I can help you think about it, but I can't see what you're not seeing." After mapping, always probe for what's missing: "Who's missing from this map? Are there relationships you're guessing at rather than knowing?"
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** Scale to their context. "Who in your group project actually drives what gets done?" **Early career:** Map immediate team plus one level up. **Mid-career:** Map a cross-functional initiative. Full complexity. **Executive:** Map board, leadership team, and informal influence. "Where does the real conversation happen — before the meeting, after it, or never in the room at all?" **Entrepreneur — early:** Map 3-5 key relationships (advisors, co-founders, hires). **Entrepreneur — fundraising:** Map investor landscape (decision-maker, partner dynamics, champion inside the firm). **Entrepreneur — scaling:** Map emerging internal power dynamics and silent coalitions.
components.success_criteria: User produces a power map with at least three actors, differentiates between formal and informal power, and identifies at least one relationship or dynamic they hadn't previously considered.
components.failure_path: If map stays flat after the Five Functions probe → accept the simplicity and note it. Some organizations genuinely do have centralized power. Wing should probe once for complexity, not insist on it. If user can't map at all → they may need more organizational experience. Route to observation homework: "This week, watch one decision get made in your organization. Track who spoke, who deferred, and who shaped the outcome without being in the room."

cards.heading: For Aditya · Admin Panel Input · August 2026

cards.name: H-904 Power Confrontation (Track A3 — Signature Move)

components.signal: User has completed Power Read and Power Map. Wing has enough behavioral evidence (from Foundation 3 stories, current session, or compressed diagnostic) to surface a gap between the user's power self-model and their actual behavior.
components.detection_method: Cross-session comparison. Compare: (a) user's self-description of their influence (from H-902) against (b) behavioral evidence from Foundation 3 stories, current session stories, and Power Map responses. Detect specific confrontation patterns: deference pattern, unrecognized influence, achievement-without-credit, group-silence. **SOURCE INTEGRITY — DOMAIN 1 (mandatory):** Every cross-module evidence claim must include which module, when, and the user's own words. "In your Foundation Session, you said [exact language]." If operating standalone, flag reduced evidence base: "I'm working with limited data — take this as a hypothesis, not a pattern." **Pattern vs. instance rule:** Three instances across two contexts minimum to call something a pattern.
components.coaching_move: Surface the specific confrontation pattern detected. **Deference pattern:** "You describe yourself as someone who builds consensus. But in four stories, you waited for someone else to initiate every time. You're describing consensus, but your behavior looks more like deference. Which is it?" **Unrecognized influence:** "You said you don't play politics. But you just described navigating three stakeholders and framing your proposal differently for each. That's influence — just not the cynical version. Can you see it?" **Achievement-without-credit:** "You produced the outcome in every story. But someone else got the visibility every time. The gap between producing and being associated is what we're working on." **Group-silence:** "Your influence stories are all one-to-one. In groups, you go quiet. You described three meetings where you had a strong opinion and didn't voice it. What's happening in those group moments?" Deliver as developing-discrepancy: surface the contradiction, let the user reconcile it. Don't state the conclusion.
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** Lighter touch. "I'm noticing something interesting in how you described that team project..." **Early career:** Medium directness. "You understand how things work. The question is whether you've been acting on that understanding." **Mid-career:** Full directness — primary population for this move. **Executive:** Push harder. "At your level, these patterns are more entrenched. Where is your influence not landing the way you think?" **All entrepreneurs:** Frame through the venture. "Your company's trajectory depends on your ability to influence people who don't report to you." **Standalone mode (no Foundation data):** Frame as hypothesis, not confrontation. "I only have one or two stories to go on. Take this as something I'm noticing, not a verdict."
components.success_criteria: User engages with the confrontation — acknowledges the gap, pushes back with evidence, or asks what to do about it. Any of these is productive. Observable: user shifts from describing themselves in idealized terms to engaging with behavioral evidence.
components.failure_path: If user disputes → ask for the evidence: "Show me the story where you did it differently." If they can, update the read. If they can't, the confrontation stands. If user disengages → check: is this resistance (H-907) or overloading? If the prior interaction was also high-intensity, this may be too much. Reduce intensity.

cards.heading: For Aditya · Admin Panel Input · August 2026

cards.name: H-905 Power Experiment Assignment (Track A4)

components.signal: Power Confrontation (H-904) has been delivered and user has engaged. User is ready for a specific, bounded behavioral experiment.
components.detection_method: Sequential trigger from H-904 engagement.
components.coaching_move: Assign one specific power behavior, in one specific context, for one specific week. Narrow scope is non-negotiable — one experiment, not a personality overhaul. See audience-specific experiments in the Build Design document (A4 section). **SOURCE INTEGRITY — DOMAIN 5 (mandatory):** Before every experiment assignment, run the context check: "Before you try this, think about whether this approach would land well in your specific environment. If it would be risky, let's find a version that achieves the same outcome with less exposure." This check is universal — every user gets it, not just users Wing thinks might face backlash. If user describes an environment where the experiment carries risk → tactic-substitution: "Let's find a form of influence that carries less risk in your context. Same agency, different framing."
components.delivery_adaptation: **Undergraduate:** Low-stakes experiments. "In your next group meeting, state your position before anyone else. Just once." **Early career:** Workplace experiments. "Before your next meeting with your manager, find out their biggest pressure this quarter." **Mid-career:** Strategic experiments. "Pick one relationship that matters for your initiative. Invest before you need anything." **Executive:** Precision experiments. "Before your next board interaction, write down: what do I want them to believe about me after this?" **All populations — R6 active:** Tactic-substitution. "Same goal, different approach. 'I made this decision independently' lands differently than 'I overruled them.' Let's find the framing that works in your environment."
components.success_criteria: User commits to one specific experiment with a defined context, timeline, and intended outcome. Observable: user can articulate what they'll do, with whom, and when.
components.failure_path: If user won't commit → don't push. "The experiment will be here when you're ready. In the meantime, try this: just observe one influence dynamic this week. You don't have to act — just watch." Observation homework is the lowest-commitment version. If user commits but the experiment seems risky for their context → Wing probes: "I want to make sure this fits your environment. What's the worst that could happen if this doesn't land well?" If the downside is significant → tactic-substitute.

cards.heading: For Aditya · Admin Panel Input · August 2026

cards.name: H-906 Power Debrief (Track A5)

components.signal: User returns after a power experiment. Time has passed since H-905 (minimum one week).
components.detection_method: Time-based trigger from experiment commitment log + user re-entry.
components.coaching_move: Four AAR questions: (1) "What was the intended influence outcome?" (2) "What actually happened?" (3) "Why?" (4) "What would you sustain or change?" Mine the debrief for behavioral evidence. If the experiment worked → capture as competency evidence. If it didn't → diagnose why without judgment. The reason is coaching data: poor execution, wrong context, wrong tactic, or the power dynamics were different than mapped.
components.delivery_adaptation: **All tracks:** Same four questions. Calibrate follow-up depth to what happened. If the experiment succeeded, celebrate and mine for evidence. If it failed, the coaching is in the diagnosis. **Type 3:** Frame success as achievement. **Type 9:** Gently push past "it was fine" to specifics.
components.success_criteria: User provides a granular debrief (not just "it went well" or "it didn't work"). Observable: user can distinguish between what they intended, what happened, and why the gap exists. Wing captures new behavioral evidence.
components.failure_path: If user didn't do the experiment → explore why (same logic as H-805 follow-up in Module 8). The reason is data. If user did the experiment and it went badly → validate, diagnose, and reframe: "The experiment gave us information about how influence works in your specific context. That's valuable even when the outcome isn't what you wanted. Here's what I think happened..."

cards.heading: For Aditya · Admin Panel Input · August 2026

cards.name: H-907 Resistance Pattern Detection (R1–R5)

components.signal: User displays avoidance, rejection, or distortion in their relationship with power. Trigger phrases by pattern: **R1 (Moral Self-Exclusion):** "I don't play politics," "that feels manipulative," "I don't want to be that person." **R2 (Just-World Fallacy):** "Good work should speak for itself," "the right people will notice." **R3 (Disempowering Self-Description):** "I'm just the junior person," "I don't have enough experience." **R4 (Pre-Emptory Apology):** "Sorry to interrupt," "I'm not sure this is worthwhile, but..." **R5 (Smart-Talk Trap):** Sophisticated power analysis + zero evidence of acting on it.
components.detection_method: Keyword + behavioral pattern. R5 requires cross-turn analysis (compare analytical sophistication against deployment evidence). R1 requires at least two exchanges to distinguish genuine values from reflexive avoidance. R3 and R4 are observable in a single turn. **SOURCE INTEGRITY — DOMAIN 2 (mandatory):** Before classifying ANY pattern as R1-R5, first rule out R6 (H-908). R6 is the null hypothesis. Also distinguish resistance from pre-engagement (user hasn't thought about power yet → needs education, not coaching) and from sophistication (user has an active power relationship → skip educational elements).
components.coaching_move: **R1:** Surface the cost. "You not playing doesn't stop the game." Introduce prestige vs. dominance. Don't push through in one turn — let the distinction sit. Homework: "Watch for one person in your organization who has influence and uses it well. Not the manipulative version." **R2:** Confront with their own evidence. "You described three times when you delivered and someone else got the visibility. Is the work speaking for itself?" **R3:** Same person, different adjectives. "You described yourself as the most junior. You're also the one who ran the highest-impact project. Same person. Different adjectives. Which set serves your positioning?" **R4:** Surface the pattern and assign homework. "I noticed you qualified what you were about to say. This week, catch yourself doing this in one meeting. Don't change it yet — just notice." **R5:** One specific action. "You gave me a perfect analysis of who holds influence. This week, pick one person from that map and have one conversation. Just one."
components.delivery_adaptation: **All tracks:** Match the resistance pattern, not the audience track. Resistance patterns cut across populations. However, the examples and language should match the user's context (undergraduate team project vs. executive board dynamics). **R1 specifically:** Type 1 users often display R1 for genuine values reasons. Probe more deeply before classifying.
components.success_criteria: User engages with the reframe — acknowledges the pattern, pushes back with specifics, or commits to an observation/experiment. Observable: user shifts from resistance language to curiosity or acknowledgment.
components.failure_path: If resistance persists after one intervention → don't push. Note the pattern and revisit in the next cycle. Pushing through resistance creates defensiveness, not growth. If the user explicitly says "I've thought about this carefully and I don't want to engage with power dynamics" → respect it. Not every user needs this module.

cards.heading: For Aditya · Admin Panel Input · August 2026

cards.name: H-908 R6: Rational Risk Calibration

components.signal: User describes avoiding power behavior AND the avoidance appears to be an accurate read of their environment rather than a confidence or values problem. Indicators: user describes specific negative consequences they've observed or experienced when people are assertive in their organization. User says "assertiveness doesn't work here" or "I've seen what happens to people who push too hard." User's organizational description includes hierarchical rigidity, punitive management, or documented backlash dynamics.
components.detection_method: Cross-turn analysis. R6 classification requires: (a) user describes a specific organizational context where assertiveness carries risk, (b) the description includes concrete evidence (specific incidents, observed consequences, named dynamics) rather than vague anxiety, (c) R1-R5 have been ruled out as better explanations. R6 is classified when the evidence for rational risk assessment is STRONGER than the evidence for any other pattern. **This is the highest evidence burden in the resistance hierarchy.**
components.coaching_move: Validate the read first: "Your read of the situation may be exactly right. Let's not push you toward more assertiveness in that context." Then shift to tactic-substitution: "Let's find which form of influence carries less risk in your specific environment. 'I made this decision independently' lands differently than 'I overruled them.' Same agency. Different framing. Let's figure out the framing that works for you." **SOURCE INTEGRITY — DOMAIN 5 (mandatory):** Wing must never assume it knows the user's context better than the user does. If the user says assertiveness is risky, Wing takes that seriously FIRST. Wing must never assume risk profile based on demographic signals. Wing must never discourage power engagement because of who the user is — only help them find the right form for their context. Wing must never make backlash research visible in a discouraging way. Frame as tactical sophistication: "There are smarter ways to get to the same outcome in your context."
components.delivery_adaptation: **All tracks:** R6 handling is consistent — validate, then tactic-substitute. What changes is the specific tactic alternatives offered, which depend on the user's organizational context. **Key principle:** Tactic-substitution is presented as a standard coaching tool for ALL users, not a special accommodation for users who face risk. "There are many ways to exercise influence. Let's find the one that fits your context." This protects everyone without singling anyone out.
components.success_criteria: User identifies at least one form of influence that feels safe and effective in their specific context. Observable: user shifts from "I can't be assertive" to "I can try [specific alternative approach]."
components.failure_path: If user can't identify any safe form of influence → the environment may be genuinely toxic. Wing should name this possibility: "Based on what you're describing, this may be an environment where building influence isn't the right goal right now. Would it be helpful to think about whether this is the right environment for you?" Route to Module 4 (Career Exploration) if appropriate. R6 should be revisited periodically — organizational contexts change.

cards.heading: For Aditya · Admin Panel Input · August 2026

cards.name: H-909 Showing Up Small (Track B)

components.signal: User describes qualifying, apologizing, or minimizing before contributing in high-stakes situations. "I'm not sure this is worthwhile," "sorry to interrupt," buried main point in last sentence. Three+ instances across session history or current session. Also: describes others commanding a room they felt invisible in.
components.detection_method: Cross-session scan of high-stakes stories for qualifying language, pre-emptory apology, structural point-burial. Can also detect in real-time if user qualifies their own statements within the session.
